newsitem.title: USA: SEC has new charges for former Centennial CEO.
newsitem.headline: SEC has new charges for former Centennial CEO.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday it has new insider trading charges against Emanuel Pinez, the former chairman and chief executive officer of Centennial Technologies Inc.

The SEC said it is alleging that Pinez engaged in "additional unlawful insider trading" through an account in the name of Felix Inc., an offshore company that the agency says holds at least $808,878 in proceeds from Pinez' sale of Centennial stock in early February.
The SEC first filed a complaint in February alleging Pinez traded in options, while knowing that the company's shares would decrease in value.
In March, Pinez was indicted on five counts of securities fraud and he has been held without bail since February on charges of insider trading.
Centennial's stock has been delisted from the New York Stock Exchange since early March. Its shares can be traded on the pink sheets.
